subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a default-off session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 lands, or should core expose activity/diagnostic signals for plugins, dashboards, and external monitoring to consume?
rationale: The request adds new Gateway/session semantics, configuration, privacy/redaction, UI/operator delivery, webhook, channel, and optional model-call behavior, so automation cannot choose the long-term product boundary safely.

options.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
options.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract and attention model are settled.

options.title: Route alerting outside core
options.body: Expose activity and diagnostics in core while plugin, ClawHub, dashboard, or external monitoring surfaces own alert delivery and summaries.

options.title: Fold into broader operator visibility
options.body: Use this issue as context for session-health and silence work but require a narrower implementation issue before coding alert behavior.

recommendation.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract and attention model are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the live prerequisite activity API issue and has recent gateway/protocol-adjacent history, making them the clearest available owner for the API/product boundary choice.
